div.head: Ger 15
div.ab: [15] Æcse, adsan, bil, byrse, scafan, sage, cimbiren, tigehoc, næfebor, mattuc, ippingiren, scear, culter ⁊ eac gadiren, siðe, sicol, weodhoc, spade, scofle, wadspitel, bærwan, besman, bytel, race, geafle, hlædre, horscamb ⁊ sceara, fyrtange, wæipundern; [15.1] ⁊ fela towtola: flexlinan, spinle, reol, gearnwindan, stodlan, lorgas, presse, pihten, timplean, wifte, wefle, wulcamb, cip, amb, crancstæf, sceaðele, seamsticcan, scearra, nædle, slic.

æcse, adsan, bil, byrse, scafan, sage, cimbiren, tigehoc, næfebor, mattuc, ippingiren, scear, culter and eac gadiren, siðe, sicol, weodhoc, spade, scofle, wadspitel, bærwan, besman, bytel, race, geafle, hlædre, horscamb and sceara, fyrtange, wæipundern. [15.1] And fela towtola: flexlinan, spinle, reol, gearnwindan, stodlan, lorgas, presse, pihten, timplean, wifte, wefle,ulcamb, cip, amb, crancstæf, sceaðele, seamsticcan, scearra, w nædle, slic.

Axt, Beil, Hippe, Bohrer, Hobel, Säge, Kimmeisen [Böttcherbeil], Ziehhaken, Naber [= Bohrer], Hacke, Brecheisen [?], Pflugschar, Kolter und auch Stachelstock, Sense, Sichel, Unkranthacke, Spaten, Schaufel, Waidhacke, Tragebahre, Besen, Stössel, Rechen, [Heu-]Gabel, Leiter, Pferdekamm und [grosse Wirthschafts-]Scheere, Feuerzange, Wage mit Gewicht; [15.1] und viele Spinngeräthe: Flachsleine, Spindel, Haspel, Garnwinde, Rietkamm des Webstuhls, Zeugbäume, [Tuch]presse, Weberkamm, Karden..?, Einschlag, Kette [oder Schiffchen], Wollkamm, Webebaum, Webespule [oder Riedblatt], Haspelstock, Schiffchen [?], ‘Saumstöcke’, kleine Scheere, Nadel, Schlägel.

[15] Axe, adze, bill, borer, plane, saw, chime-iron [cooper's axe], drawing-hook, auger, mattock, crowbar[?], ploughshare, coulter and also goad, scythe, sickle, weed-hook, spade, shovel, woad-dibble, barrow, broom, beetle, rake, [hay-]fork, ladder, horse-comb and [large household] shears, fire-tongs, scales with weights; [15.1] and many spinning implements: flax-line, spindle, reel, yarn-winder, stodles [loom uprights], beams, press, comb, carders(?), weft, warp [or shuttle], wool-comb, loom-roller, slay [or reed], winding-stick, shuttle[?], seam-sticks, small shears, needle, beater.

Axe, adze, billhook, chisel, plane, saw, joining iron, hook for earthenware vessels, auger, mattock, crowbar, ploughshare, coulter, and also a goad, scythe, sickle, weed-hook (hoe), spade, shovel, woad-dibble, barrow, broom, mallet, rake, fork, ladder, horse-comb, scissors, fire tongs, weighing scale and many spinning implements, a cord for hanging flax from, spindle, reel, yarn winder, weaver’s slay, distaff, clothes’ press, loom parts, [weavers’ instrument], [weavers’ instrument], [weavers’ instrument], wool comb, weaver’s beam, pail, [weaver’s instrument], shuttle, harness, [weaver’s instrument], shears, needle, mallet.

ax, adze, billhook, chisel, plane, saw, clamp, pull hook, auger, mattock, crowbar, plowshare, coulter, and likewise a goad, scythe, sickle, hoe, spade, shovel, woad dibble, barrow, broom, mallet, rake, fork, ladder, horse comb and shears, fire tongs, scale. [15.1] Also many spinning tools: a line for hanging flax, spindle, reel, yarn winders, loom uprights, heddle rods, a cloth press, comb beater, temples, weft thread, warp thread, wool comb, yoke beam, beater, crank, sheath, seam picks, fabric shears, needle, wooden mallet.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 15–15.1. B's ‘næfebor’ stands so. Liebermann's translations of the rarer terms are marked with queries; the English follows his German.; AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 336 / 337, October 2026 (was “[15.1]”, now “∅”)
This row holds several of Rabin’s sections (15, 15.1), each marked with its number.

spinning tools: The implements listed here have occasioned considerable critical head-scratching. Though some are recognizable tools still in use, others remain obscure. The confusion is exacerbated by the fact that many of the terms in this list occur nowhere else in Old English.

note.seg: sic

Die ersten Wörter der Liste beginnen mit a-, b-; vgl. 17{c}.—Nicht ‘Schwert’ (Sweet, Kluge); vgl. Toller Suppl., noch jetzt bill: ‘Haumesser, Sichelhacke’; auch mengl.: Mätzner.—‘Axt, Krummaxt, Beil’ Sk-Wi
The first words of the list begin with a-, b-; cf. 17{c}.—Not ‘sword’ (Sweet, Kluge); cf. Toller Suppl.; still today bill: ‘chopper, bill-hook’; also ME: Mätzner.—‘axe, curved axe, hatchet’ Sk-Wi
So Sweet, Kluge; doch neben foratorium glossiert das Wort auch scalprum, scalpellum ‘Ahle [so Sk-Wi], Lanzette, Meissel, Gartenmesser’; s. Toller Suppl. s. v. byres
So Sweet, Kluge; but besides foratorium the word also glosses scalprum, scalpellum ‘awl [so Sk-Wi], lancet, chisel, pruning-knife’; see Toller Suppl. s. v. byres
‘joining-iron, clamp [Schraubzwinge]?’ Toller Suppl.; ‘edge-iron?’ Sweet; kimme, chimbe (mengl., chimb) ‘oberer Fassrand’; kimisern mndd. ‘Böttcherbeil’; Lübben. Fehlt Sk-Wi
‘joining-iron, clamp [screw-clamp]?’ Toller Suppl.; ‘edge-iron?’ Sweet; kimme, chimbe (ME, chimb) ‘upper rim of a cask’; kimisern MLG ‘cooper's axe’; Lübben. Not in Sk-Wi
‘Zughaken’ Kluge
‘draw-hook’ Kluge
Vgl. Kluge Etymol. Wb. s. v. naber. ‘Besen [?], Hacken, Harken [?]’ Sk-Wi
Cf. Kluge Etymol. Wb. s. v. naber. ‘broom [?], hoes, rakes [?]’ Sk-Wi
‘crowbar’ Toller, Sweet; cipping iren ‘Zimmerereisen’ (vgl. nengl. to chip) will emendieren Ritter o. 12³
‘crowbar’ Toller, Sweet; Ritter above 12³ would emend to cipping iren ‘carpenter's iron’ (cf. Mod. Engl. to chip)
Nicht ‘Pflugschar’, sondern das krumme Messer ‘Sech’ davor; vgl. Toller, auch Suppl.
Not ‘ploughshare’, but the curved knife in front of it, the ‘coulter’; cf. Toller, also Suppl.
So Kluge; vgl. jetzt goad; gadiren glossiert aculeus, stimulus
So Kluge; cf. today goad; gadiren glosses aculeus, stimulus
S. o. 10{q}. Noch jetzt spittle; mengl. spitel (Stratmann); ‘Waidpflanzer’ [?] Sk-Wi
See above 10{q}. Still today spittle; ME spitel (Stratmann); ‘woad-planter’ [?] Sk-Wi
‘barrow’ Toller Suppl., ‘wheelbarrow’ Sweet, ‘Schubkarren’ Sk-Wi, ‘Trage’ Mätzner, nicht mit Kluge ‘Korb’
‘barrow’ Toller Suppl., ‘wheelbarrow’ Sweet, ‘wheelbarrow’ Sk-Wi, ‘hand-barrow’ Mätzner; not, with Kluge, ‘basket’
Jetzt beetle ‘Schlägel, Rammstock’; ‘Hammer’ Toller Suppl., ‘Stampfe’ Kluge, ‘Schwinge’ Sk-Wi
Now beetle ‘mallet, rammer’; ‘hammer’ Toller Suppl., ‘stamper’ Kluge, ‘swingle’ Sk-Wi
Nicht ‘Gabel, fork’ im Sinne von furca Vinogradoff Villain. 170; jetzt gaffle ‘Mist(usw.)gabel’
Not ‘fork’ in the sense of furca, Vinogradoff Villain. 170; now gaffle ‘dung (etc.) fork’
Zum Scheren von Tieren und Pflanzen; Toller 824b
For shearing animals and plants; Toller 824b
Abbildung aus Agsächs. Kalender 11. Jhs.: Heyne Deut. Wohn. 34
Illustration from an Anglo-Saxon calendar of the 11th cent.: Heyne Deut. Wohn. 34
‘pair of scales’ Sweet; ‘steelyard’ Toller. Nicht ‘Gewicht’ (Kluge), obwohl pundar : perpendiculum glossiert; Toller. Mittelengl. punder: ‘Wage’
‘pair of scales’ Sweet; ‘steelyard’ Toller. Not ‘weight’ (Kluge), although there is the gloss pundar : perpendiculum; Toller. Middle English punder: ‘balance’
S. Gl Weberei, die vor 1066 nur häuslich war; Cunningham 179⁵.—‘Werkzeug’ Kluge zu weit; s. Composita towcræft, -hus, -lic, -myderce
See Gl Weberei, which before 1066 was purely domestic; Cunningham 179⁵.—‘tool’ Kluge too wide; see the compounds towcræft, -hus, -lic, -myderce
‘Seil’ Kluge; spirae glossiert line (Ælfric); ‘reel’ Sweet; allein dies ist das hier folgende reol; ‘Flachswinde’ Sk-Wi
‘rope’ Kluge; line glosses spirae (Ælfric); ‘reel’ Sweet; but that is the reol that follows here; ‘flax-reel’ Sk-Wi
Mätzner 335
Mätzner 335
Mittelengl. telarium, lame de tisserant glossiert, jetzt studdles; ‘slay’ Toller, Sweet; unerklärt Sk
In Middle English it glosses telarium, lame de tisserant, now studdles; ‘slay’ Toller, Sweet; unexplained Sk
Glossiert colus, webbeam, liciatorium (Ælfric); ‘weaver's beam’ Toller, Sweet; ‘Spindel’ Kluge
Glosses colus, webbeam, liciatorium (Ælfric); ‘weaver's beam’ Toller, Sweet; ‘spindle’ Kluge
Mittelengl. pannicipium, vestiplicium glossiert
In Middle English it glosses pannicipium, vestiplicium
pecten glossiert
Glosses pecten
Nach Ritter (o. 12³) dt. tempel ‘Sperrute, Spannstock, Breithalter’
According to Ritter (above 12³) German tempel ‘spreading rod, stretcher, temple’
‘weft’ Sweet, Toller; fehlt Sk
‘weft’ Sweet, Toller; not in Sk
= ‘Aufzug’ (Kluge), ‘warp’ (Sweet); ‘weft’ Toller, wie md. wefel, wevel ‘Einschlag’ [so Sk-Wi] heisst. Aber es glossiert panniculae, d. i. panuclium ‘Weberschiffchen’. ‘Aufwinder’ Sk-Wi
= ‘warp’ (Kluge), ‘warp’ (Sweet); ‘weft’ Toller, as Middle German wefel, wevel means ‘weft’ [so Sk-Wi]. But it glosses panniculae, i.e. panuclium ‘weaver's shuttle’. ‘winder’ Sk-Wi

‘Webespule’ Kluge; ‘reed (Sweet) or slay’ [so Sk-Wi] Bo-Toller; Toller Suppl. identifiziert es mit dem cautere [Brenneisen] glossierenden Worte: das passt nicht. Camb emendiert Brasch Werkzeuge 59, m. E. unnötig, wenn auch das Vorkommen von camb hinter 17¹⁸ keinen Gegengrund bietet

‘weaving-bobbin’ Kluge; ‘reed (Sweet) or slay’ [so Sk-Wi] Bo-Toller; Toller Suppl. identifies it with the word glossing cautere [branding-iron]: that does not fit. Brasch Werkzeuge 59 emends to Camb, in my opinion unnecessarily, even though the occurrence of camb after 17¹⁸ offers no argument against it
‘Webstock?’ Kluge; crank noch jetzt; ‘Weife, Haspel, Kurbel, reel for winding thread’ Mätzner, Stratmann, Halliwell; ‘Wickler mit gebogenem Griff’ Sk-Wi
‘weaving-stick?’ Kluge; crank still today; ‘reel, windlass, crank, reel for winding thread’ Mätzner, Stratmann, Halliwell; ‘winder with a curved handle’ Sk-Wi
Nach Ritter (o. 12³) anord. skeið; ‘slay or weaver's rod’; ‘skuttle?’ Toller, ‘Weberschiff’ Sk-Wi; dies lautet mengl. scitil, schitel; Stratmann, Skeat
According to Ritter (above 12³) ON skeið; ‘slay or weaver's rod’; ‘skuttle?’ Toller, ‘weaver's shuttle’ Sk-Wi; in ME this is scitil, schitel; Stratmann, Skeat
Ich übersetze nur silbenhaft.—‘Nahthalter’ Sk-Wi
I translate only syllable by syllable.—‘seam-holder’ Sk-Wi
‘Hammer’ Kluge; ‘sleekstone’ [Glättstein; Sk-Wi] fürs Tuch Sweet, Toller; vgl. Bateson Records of Leicester I 71
‘hammer’ Kluge; ‘sleekstone’ [smoothing-stone; Sk-Wi] for the cloth Sweet, Toller; cf. Bateson Records of Leicester I 71
